name: Isomethadone
summary: A rare pharmaceutical drug known as isoamidone, this opioid analgesic and methadone analogue was withdrawn from the market and is seldom seen today. Rarely abused, reports state it is around 2x potentcy of methadone, and reports indicate euphoric effects.

pharmacology.text: It binds to and activates both the μ- and δ-opioid receptors, with the (S)-isomer being the more potent of the two enantiomers.

uses.text: Isomethadone (INN, BAN; trade name Liden; also known as isoamidone) is a synthetic opioid analgesic and antitussive related to methadone that was used formerly as a pharmaceutical drug but is now no longer marketed. Isomethadone was used as both an analgesic and antitussive.
